Dual-kVp Rapid-Switching Virtual Monoenergetic Imaging

One rotation of a GE Revolution Apex Elite that switches between 80 and 140 kVp becomes virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) at 50, 70, 100 and 140 keV, checked rod by rod against theory.

The scanner, the acquisition and the chain are those of the basis-spectral-denoising paper: its GE model and physics switches, the two exposures of a rotation with their duty cycles, view integration, its fitted pair of FDK windows and a calibration draw that fixes the spectral pair.

The Chain at a Glance

Each exposure is projected once and drawn three times: the noise-free expectation, the measured scan and a calibration scan. The measured counts of both kVp go through one call, BS.vmi_pipeline. Both channels stay separate all the way into the likelihood; nothing is rebinned into one "effective" spectrum. The noise-free draw goes through the same reconstruction, without the denoising, and is the reference every result is scored against.

begin
    """A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
    function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
        ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
        Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
        Mke.hidespines!(ax)
        Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
        return ax
    end

    """The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
    function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
        r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
        arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
            Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
            for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
        ]
        return vcat(
            arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
            arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
            arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
            arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
        )
    end

    """A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
    function arrow!(
        ax,
        a,
        b;
        color = COLORS.muted,
        linewidth = 2.5,
        head = 15,
        linestyle = :solid,
    )
        a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
        Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
        t = b - a
        Mke.scatter!(
            ax,
            [b];
            marker = :utriangle,
            markersize = head,
            rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
            color,
            markerspace = :pixel,
        )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
    `subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
    """
    function node!(
        ax,
        c,
        title;
        subtitle = "",
        w = 3.0,
        h = 1.0,
        accent = COLORS.violet,
        fill = COLORS.card,
        textcolor = COLORS.ink,
        subcolor = COLORS.muted,
        titlesize = 19,
        subtitlesize = 15,
        code = false,
    )
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
            color = fill,
            strokecolor = accent,
            strokewidth = 2,
        )
        strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
        Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
        font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
        dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] + dy;
            text = title,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = titlesize,
            font,
            color = textcolor,
        )
        isempty(subtitle) ||
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                c[1] + 0.05,
                c[2] - 0.22 * h;
                text = subtitle,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = subtitlesize,
                color = subcolor,
            )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
    optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
    `labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
    """
    function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
        ax = canvas(position, limits)
        box(key) = nodes[key]
        function port(from, to)
            a, b = box(from), box(to)
            if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # side by side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
                # one above the other
                s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
                return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
            else
                # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            end
        end
        for (from, to) in edges
            p, q = port(from, to)
            if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # straight across or straight down
                arrow!(ax, p, q)
            else
                # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
                mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
                Mke.lines!(
                    ax,
                    Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                    linewidth = 2.5,
                )
                arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
            end
            haskey(labels, from => to) &&
                Mke.text!(
                    ax,
                    (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                    q[2] + 0.12;
                    text = labels[from => to],
                    align = (:center, :bottom),
                    fontsize = 15,
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                )
        end
        for (_, n) in nodes
            node!(
                ax,
                (n[1], n[2]),
                n[3];
                subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
                accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
                w,
                h,
            )
        end
        return ax
    end

    """
    A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
    of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
    of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
    """
    function gantry!(
        ax;
        sid = 5.4,
        sdd = 9.5,
        angles = (90.0,),
        fan_deg = 50.0,
        r_object = 2.0,
        detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
        labels = ("Tube",),
        dark = true,
        object = true,
    )
        ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
        ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
            color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
        )
        for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
            θ = deg2rad(θ)
            s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
            half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
            # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
            edge = Mke.Point2f[
                s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
                for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
            ]
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
                color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
                strokewidth = 0,
            )
            Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                s * 1.18;
                text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 17,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
        object &&
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
                color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
                strokecolor = ink,
                strokewidth = 1.5,
            )
        return ax
    end

    """
    The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
    `limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
    draw into them, then show the figure.
    """
    function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
        fig = Mke.Figure(;
            size,
            backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
            figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
        )
        axes = [
            canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
            for i in eachindex(titles)
        ]
        for i in eachindex(titles)
            Mke.Label(
                fig[2, i],
                titles[i];
                fontsize = 25,
                font = :bold,
                color = COLORS.night_ink,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
            Mke.Label(
                fig[3, i],
                subtitles[i];
                fontsize = 17,
                color = COLORS.night_muted,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
        end
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
        return fig, axes
    end
end;

KVP_COLORS = (low = COLORS.beam, high = COLORS.violet);
gammex_layout

The Gammex 472 as the drawings show it: its body radius and every rod's centre and radius (cm, about the centre of the image), measured from the phantom's own label mask.

"""
The Gammex 472 as the drawings show it: its body radius and every rod's centre and radius
(cm, about the centre of the image), measured from the phantom's own label mask.
"""
function gammex_layout(phantom)
    mask = phantom.mask[:, :, (size(phantom.mask, 3) + 1) ÷ 2]
    voxel = phantom.voxel_size[1]
    centre = (size(mask, 1) + 1) / 2
    function rod(label)
        pixels = findall(==(UInt8(label)), mask)
        return (
            x = (mean(p -> p[1], pixels) - centre) * voxel,
            y = (mean(p -> p[2], pixels) - centre) * voxel,
            r = sqrt(length(pixels) / π) * voxel,
        )
    end
    return (
        body = sqrt(count(!=(0x00), mask) / π) * voxel,
        voxel = voxel,
        Ca = [rod(label) for label in 10:16],
        I = [rod(label) for label in 20:26],
        Ca_names = ["50", "100", "200", "300", "400", "500", "600"],
        I_names = ["2", "2.5", "5", "7.5", "10", "15", "20"],
    )
end
gammex!

Draws the Gammex 472 of layout on ax: the solid-water body, calcium rods in red and iodine rods in green. show picks what stands out: :all, :water (with region, a mask on the phantom's image grid, drawn in cyan), :Ca or :I (those rods, named by concentration, each with its ROI of radius roi cm); the rest is faded.

"""
Draws the Gammex 472 of `layout` on `ax`: the solid-water body, calcium rods in red and iodine
rods in green. `show` picks what stands out: `:all`, `:water` (with `region`, a mask on the
phantom's image grid, drawn in cyan), `:Ca` or `:I` (those rods, named by concentration, each with
its ROI of radius `roi` cm); the rest is faded.
"""
function gammex!(ax, layout; show = :all, region = nothing, roi = 0.55, dark = false)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    faded(group) = show in (:all, group) ? 1.0 : 0.25
    disk(x, y, r) = Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(x, y), r)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        disk(0, 0, layout.body);
        color = (COLORS.blue, show == :water ? 0.25 : 0.55),
        strokecolor = ink,
        strokewidth = 1.5,
    )
    if show == :water && region !== nothing
        xs = ((1:size(region, 1)) .- (size(region, 1) + 1) / 2) .* layout.voxel
        ys = ((1:size(region, 2)) .- (size(region, 2) + 1) / 2) .* layout.voxel
        Mke.heatmap!(
            ax,
            xs,
            ys,
            [inside ? 1.0f0 : NaN32 for inside in region];
            colormap = [COLORS.cyan, COLORS.cyan],
            colorrange = (0, 1),
            nan_color = :transparent,
        )
    end
    for (group, color) in ((:Ca, COLORS.red), (:I, COLORS.green))
        rods = getfield(layout, group)
        names = getfield(layout, Symbol(group, :_names))
        offset = group == :Ca ? 2.3 : 2.6
        for (rod, name) in zip(rods, names)
            Mke.poly!(ax, disk(rod.x, rod.y, rod.r); color = (color, faded(group)))
            show == group || continue
            Mke.lines!(
                ax,
                disk(rod.x, rod.y, roi);
                color = COLORS.paper,
                linewidth = 2,
                linestyle = :dash,
            )
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                rod.x * (1 + offset / hypot(rod.x, rod.y)),
                rod.y * (1 + offset / hypot(rod.x, rod.y));
                text = name,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 15,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
    end
    return ax
end
kvp_switching!

Rapid kVp switching on ax (a canvas about (0, 12.6, -1.6, 7.6)): the tube voltage over three view periods, 80 kVp for duty of each and 140 kVp for the rest.

"""
Rapid kVp switching on `ax` (a canvas about `(0, 12.6, -1.6, 7.6)`): the tube voltage over three
view periods, 80 kVp for `duty` of each and 140 kVp for the rest.
"""
function kvp_switching!(ax; duty = 0.65, dark = false)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    muted = dark ? COLORS.night_muted : COLORS.muted
    period, low, high = 4.0, 1.8, 5.0
    for v in 0:2
        t0 = 0.6 + v * period
        t1 = t0 + duty * period
        t2 = t0 + period
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Rect2f(t0, 0, t1 - t0, low); color = (KVP_COLORS.low, 0.55))
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Rect2f(t1, 0, t2 - t1, high); color = (KVP_COLORS.high, 0.55))
        Mke.lines!(
            ax,
            Mke.Point2f[(t0, low), (t1, low), (t1, high), (t2, high), (t2, low)];
            color = ink,
            linewidth = 2.5,
        )
        Mke.lines!(ax, [t2, t2], [-0.25, 0.0]; color = muted, linewidth = 2)
    end
    arrow!(ax, (0.6, 0), (12.9, 0); color = muted, head = 12)
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        12.9,
        -0.35;
        text = "Time",
        align = (:right, :top),
        fontsize = 16,
        color = muted,
    )
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        0.6 + duty * period / 2,
        low / 2;
        text = "80 kVp",
        align = (:center, :center),
        fontsize = 17,
        font = :bold,
        color = ink,
    )
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        0.6 + period * (1 + duty) / 2,
        high / 2 + 0.6;
        text = "140\nkVp",
        align = (:center, :center),
        fontsize = 17,
        font = :bold,
        color = ink,
    )
    # one view period, bracketed
    Mke.lines!(
        ax,
        Mke.Point2f[(4.6, 5.6), (4.6, 5.9), (8.6, 5.9), (8.6, 5.6)];
        color = muted,
        linewidth = 2,
    )
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        6.6,
        6.1;
        text = "One View: $(round(Int, 100duty)) % + $(round(Int, 100(1 - duty))) %",
        align = (:center, :bottom),
        fontsize = 16,
        color = muted,
    )
    return ax
end

1. The Phantom

The Gammex 472 multi-energy phantom: a solid-water body with seven calcium (50–600 mg/mL) and seven iodine (2–20 mg/mL) rods, 1 cm thick and the same at every z. The label mask goes to the GPU; its material table stays on the host.

phantom_cpu = BS.create_gammex_472(
    n_voxels = 512,
    n_slices = 16,
    fov_cm = 35.0,
    z_cm = 1.0,
);
phantom = BS.Phantom(
    to_gpu(phantom_cpu.mask),
    phantom_cpu.materials,
    phantom_cpu.voxel_size,
    phantom_cpu.origin,
    phantom_cpu.extent,
);
# where the body and every rod are, for the drawings
GAMMEX = gammex_layout(phantom_cpu);

2. The Scanner and Its kVp Switching

The documented REVOLUTION_APEX: source–isocentre 625.6 mm, source–detector 1100 mm, 834 columns × 0.6 mm on an arc with the quarter-detector offset, 256 rows × 0.625 mm, a Gemstone scintillator (:lumex) and the GE large-body bowtie. Here without electronic noise.

Rapid kVp switching alternates one tube between 80 and 140 kVp within every view period, so both channels see the same rays on one detector. It is modelled as two co-registered acquisitions on this one geometry, each with its share of the view period, its duty cycle: 0.65 at 80 kVp, 0.35 at 140 kVp. A channel's tube current is the instantaneous current times its duty cycle, and its views integrate over that fraction of the arc the gantry turns per view (view_arc).

3. Two Exposures and Their Dose

One protocol per exposure: 984 views over a 0.5 s rotation, 5 mm collimation, 4.5 mm of added aluminium on both. The physical scan ran 407 mA at 80 kVp and 405 mA at 140 kVp, each multiplied by its duty cycle.

The simulator's tube output per mA is generic, not GE's, so one factor, DOSE_SCALE, scales both currents: it keeps the split between the exposures and makes the simulated CTDIvol (the package's Monte Carlo dose in the 32 cm body phantom, summed over the exposures) equal the 10.07 mGy the physical scan reported. The noise is then that of the dose the physical scan delivered.

# The two exposures of one rotation: each energy is read for its duty cycle of the view
# period, the fraction of the view's arc it integrates over and of its tube current. Each has
# its own noise seed: two acquisitions drawn from one seed would carry the same noise pattern,
# correlated between the channels, which a real scan never has.
exposures = (
    low = (
        label = "80 kVp",
        kVp = 80,
        mA = 407 * 0.65,
        view_arc = 0.65,
        seed = 1234,
        filters = [("Al", 4.5)],
    ),
    high = (
        label = "140 kVp",
        kVp = 140,
        mA = 405 * 0.35,
        view_arc = 0.35,
        seed = 4321,
        filters = [("Al", 4.5)],
    ),
);
begin
    "The `CTProtocol` of exposure `e`, its tube current scaled by `mA_scale`."
    exposure_protocol(e; mA_scale = 1.0) = BS.CTProtocol(
        kVp = e.kVp,
        mA = e.mA * mA_scale,
        views = 984,
        rotation_time = 0.5,
        collimation_mm = 5.0,
        additional_filters = e.filters,
    )
    "The CTDIvol (mGy, 32 cm body phantom) of `protocol` on `scanner`."
    ctdi_vol(protocol) = BS.compute_dose(
        BS.dose_source(scanner, protocol),
        protocol,
    ).ctdi_vol_mGy
end;

DOSE_SCALE = 10.07 / sum(e -> ctdi_vol(exposure_protocol(e)), exposures)
protocols = map(e -> exposure_protocol(e; mA_scale = DOSE_SCALE), exposures);

4. Physics, Draws and the Image Grid

The physics switches of the basis-spectral-denoising GE model: every effect of the energy-integrating path on except optical crosstalk, and the detector efficiency from the Monte Carlo table of the Lumex scintillator (the scanner's default, detector_efficiency_mode = :mc_lut).

DrawNoiseUsed for
0, referenceoffthe noise-free expectation every result is scored against
1, measuredonevery result below
9, calibrationonfixing the spectral pair, never scored

The reconstruction grid is the clinical series': 8 slices of 0.625 mm over the central 5 mm, 512² over 35 cm.

<details><summary><strong>Why <code>view_samples = 5</code>: view integration</strong></summary>

A detector integrates while the gantry turns, so each view records the transmitted intensity averaged over the arc it sweeps, r · view_arc · Δθ at radius r: a blur of the object, largest far from the isocentre, that the noise, counted once per view, does not share. view_samples = 5 samples that arc with five sub-views (the midpoint rule), 0.2 mm apart at the edge of a 35 cm field. Without it the simulated signal is sharper, relative to its noise, than a physical scanner's, and no reconstruction window can match both the physical resolution and the physical noise texture.

</details>

begin
    VIEW_SAMPLES = 5
    ge_opts = BS.SimOptions(projector = :dd_fast, view_samples = VIEW_SAMPLES)
    "The same physics switches with one field replaced."
    with_option(opts, field, value) = BS.SimOptions(;
        (f => getfield(opts, f) for f in fieldnames(BS.SimOptions) if f !== field)...,
        (field => value,)...,
    )
end;
begin
    # Draw 0 is the noise-free expectation; draw r ≥ 1 gives each exposure the seed
    # `seed + 1000 (r − 1)`, so the exposures stay independent within a draw and the draws of
    # each other (basis-spectral-denoising's seeds for the Gammex).
    DRAWS = (reference = 0, measured = 1, calibration = 9)
    realization_seed(e, r) = e.seed + 1000 * (max(r, 1) - 1)
    "The options of draw `r` of exposure `e`: its seed, its noise, its arc."
    draw_opts(e, r) = with_option(
        with_option(with_option(ge_opts, :seed, realization_seed(e, r)), :use_noise, r > 0),
        :view_arc,
        e.view_arc,
    )
end;
recon_opts = let
    slice_thickness_mm = 0.625
    n_recon_slices = round(Int, 5.0 / slice_thickness_mm)
    BS.ReconOptions(matrix_size = (512, 512, n_recon_slices), fov_cm = 35.0, z_cm = 0.5)
end;

5. Simulate the Two Exposures: simulate!

Each exposure is projected once. The noise-free draw runs first with keep_projection = true, which returns everything before the noise; the measured and calibration draws pass it back (projection) and only draw their noise, bit-identical to simulating each afresh at a fraction of the cost.

Each acquisition keeps its corrected log sinograms and its one-channel spectral basis, spectral_basis(ws, protocol): each ray's detected spectrum (source × filtration × bowtie × the detector's signal per photon, m₁(E) = E·efficiency(E)), the model the projector applied, scaled to the ray's noise-equivalent quanta in air, I₀·ff·S₁²/S₂. An energy integrator's signal is not Poisson: its variance is S₂/S₁ times its mean, the dispersion, which rises as the beam hardens.

simulate_exposure

Simulates the three draws of exposure e under protocol, projecting once: each draw's sinogram, the wall time, and the acquisition's geometry and one-channel spectral basis.

"""
Simulates the three draws of exposure `e` under `protocol`, projecting once: each draw's
sinogram, the wall time, and the acquisition's geometry and one-channel spectral basis.
"""
function simulate_exposure(e, protocol)
    @info "Simulating dual-kVp channel: $(e.label)"
    channels = Dict{Int, Array{Float32, 3}}()
    projection = nothing
    model = nothing
    elapsed_s = @elapsed for r in (DRAWS.reference, DRAWS.measured, DRAWS.calibration)
        opts = draw_opts(e, r)
        ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, opts, recon_opts, phantom)
        try
            result = BS.simulate!(
                ws,
                phantom,
                protocol,
                opts;
                report_dose = false,
                keep_projection = projection === nothing,
                projection,
            )
            projection === nothing && (projection = result.projection)
            channels[r] = Float32.(Array(ws.sinogram))
            if model === nothing
                # the acquisition's one-channel basis: the model the projector applied
                model = (geom = ws.geom, basis = BS.spectral_basis(ws, protocol))
            end
        finally
            BS.release_backend!(ws)
        end
    end
    return (; label = e.label, channels, elapsed_s, model...)
end
dual_scans = [simulate_exposure(exposures[k], protocols[k]) for k in keys(exposures)];

The three draws of the two exposures took 64.0 s for 80 kVp and 2.8 s for 140 kVp, one projection each. Each sinogram is 834 × 12 × 984 (columns × rows × views).

6. Two Spectra on Every Ray

spectral_basis_from_acquisitions merges the two kVp energy grids onto their union and scales each acquisition's per-ray spectrum by its own noise-equivalent quanta, so the likelihood sees the absolute response $\Phi_k(E)$ of every ray and channel: source, filtration, bowtie and detector, the model that generated the data. It does not depend on the noise, so every draw shares it.

basis = BS.spectral_basis_from_acquisitions(acquisitions = [s.basis for s in dual_scans]);

The basis holds 2 channels on a 274-point energy grid, 4 to 140 keV, for 834 × 12 rays; the response sums to the air counts to within 3.2e-8 (relative).

7. The Chain's Settings

The denoiser is generalized HYPR-LR in both domains, BS.SpectralHYPR(). Before the decomposition it pools a 3 × 3 (column × view) window on the counts of each detector row, over views of one parity so the odd- and even-view halves stay independent, with each channel's dispersion measured on the air rays. After the reconstruction it pools the complement of the basis pair within each slice, over the window with the least estimated risk. Neither ever pools across detector rows or slices. The decomposition is the K-channel estimator with its published controls; T-LBF (a photon-counting filter) is off; the view-direction antialias is on; ACNR is on (vmi_pipeline's default).

A pair of FDK windows. A VMI is $A(E)\,M + B(E)\,I_\perp$: $M$ is the minimum-noise VMI (the composite, at $E^\star$) and $I_\perp$ its complement, whose noise is uncorrelated with $M$'s. BS.PairFilter gives each its own window, and one pair serves every energy. Each window is an apodized ramp $W(f) = \exp(-(f/f_c)^p)$ on the grid-Nyquist axis, the GE pair fitted by basis-spectral-denoising to the physical Gammex scan's MTF at every energy and NPS shape, on this notebook's grid.

Why not one window per basis image?

The water and iodine images' noise is strongly anti-correlated, and cancels in a VMI only where both were filtered alike. A window per basis image would leave uncancelled noise in every VMI wherever the two windows differ; the composite and its complement have no such correlation to break.

projectionkernelHYPRKernel(3 × 3, local linear)dispersion:measuredview_stride2imagecandidates132537411515621731841noise_window15
# the published denoiser: ProjectionHYPR(3 × 3 box, view_stride = 2) and ImageHYPR()
HYPR_CHAIN = BS.SpectralHYPR()
VMI_CHAIN = (
    method = :nchannel,
    controls = BS.NChannelControls(),
    use_tlbf = false,
    antialias = true,
);
# The GE pair of basis-spectral-denoising (`RECON.ge`): W(f) = exp(-(f / f_c)^p) at 11 knots.
GE_KERNELS = (composite = (fc = 0.55, p = 1.5), complement = (fc = 1.05, p = 1.0));
PAIR_FILTER = let knots = Tuple(range(0.0, 1.0, length = 11))
    window(q) = BS.CustomFilter(
        knots,
        Tuple(round(exp(-(x / q.fc)^q.p), digits = 5) for x in knots)
    )
    BS.PairFilter(window(GE_KERNELS.composite), window(GE_KERNELS.complement))
end;

8. The Calibration Draw: pair_basis and composite_energy

The pair the windows act on, $(E^\star, \beta)$, and the energy of the composite that ACNR and the image-domain HYPR act on are properties of the scanner and protocol. They are measured once, on the calibration draw, and fixed for every other draw, as basis-spectral-denoising's PAIR_BASIS does:

  1. the calibration draw is decomposed as measured, and after the projection-domain HYPR alone (vmi_pipeline(; keep_sinograms = true), with SpectralHYPR(image = nothing) for the second);

  2. BS.spectral_pair of the first, with a standard soft-tissue window, gives the minimum-noise energy $E^\star$ and the complement $\beta$: the pair_basis;

  3. BS.spectral_pair of the second on that basis gives the minimum-noise energy after the projection-domain HYPR, which moves it: the composite_energy.

Near its minimum the VMI noise hardly changes with energy, so the argmin of one acquisition is itself noise and would move from draw to draw. Measured on a draw of its own, it cannot tune the chain to the draw being scored, and the noise-free reference, which has no noise to measure it from, is reconstructed with the same pair as the measured scan.

pair_basisEstar83.0β-0.0189128composite_energy80.0
calibration = let
    geom = first(dual_scans).geom
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size
    channels = [s.channels[DRAWS.calibration] for s in dual_scans]
    decompose(denoiser) = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
        channels,
        basis,
        geom,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        matrix_size,
        denoiser,
        keep_sinograms = true,
        use_acnr = false,
        VMI_CHAIN...,
    ).sinograms
    pair(d; kw...) = BS.spectral_pair(
        d.water,
        d.iodine,
        geom,
        matrix_size;
        filter = BS.SoftFilter(),
        antialias = VMI_CHAIN.antialias,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        kw...,
    )
    x = pair(decompose(nothing))
    c = pair(
        decompose(BS.SpectralHYPR(image = nothing));
        basis = (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β),
    )
    (pair_basis = (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β), composite_energy = c.Estar)
end

9. One Call: vmi_pipeline

From the two measured sinograms to the VMI stack, reconstructed on the notebook's grid (recon_opts.matrix_size) with every detector row kept: the published chain, with the GE windows and the calibration draw's pair.

dual_vmi = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
    channels = [s.channels[DRAWS.measured] for s in dual_scans],
    basis,
    geom = first(dual_scans).geom,
    to_backend = to_gpu,
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
    vmi_energies = (50.0, 70.0, 100.0, 140.0),
    denoiser = HYPR_CHAIN,
    fbp_filter = PAIR_FILTER,
    pair_basis = calibration.pair_basis,
    composite_energy = calibration.composite_energy,
    VMI_CHAIN...,
);

The noise-free reference is the noise-free draw through the same reconstruction, windows and pair, with nothing to denoise: no HYPR and no ACNR. Scoring the measured VMIs against it measures what the noise and the denoising do, separately from what the physics the decomposition does not invert exactly (scatter, and the blurs of the focal spot, the detector and the view integration) does to both.

reference_vmi = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
    channels = [s.channels[DRAWS.reference] for s in dual_scans],
    basis,
    geom = first(dual_scans).geom,
    to_backend = to_gpu,
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
    vmi_energies = (50.0, 70.0, 100.0, 140.0),
    fbp_filter = PAIR_FILTER,
    pair_basis = calibration.pair_basis,
    composite_energy = calibration.composite_energy,
    use_acnr = false,
    VMI_CHAIN...,
);

10. Basis Images and VMIs

The water and iodine basis pair after ACNR and the image HYPR (mid slice), and the VMIs synthesized from it. Every VMI comes from this one pair; no energy-dependent filtering is applied to any of them.

11. Accuracy and Noise

Per-rod measured, noise-free and theoretical HU at the four VMI energies, the water region's mean and noise, and the regression of measured on theoretical HU.

QuantityHow it is measured
measured HUthe mean over an 8-pixel-radius disk at each rod's centroid, over every slice, of the measured VMIs
noise-free HUthe same mean on the noise-free reference
theoretical HU$1000\,(\mu_r(E) - \mu_w(E))/\mu_w(E)$ of the rod's material, from BS.compute_μ_at_energy, with no fitting
water regionthe solid water eroded with erode_mask_2d(…; erode_px = 12): its mask blurred by a 12-pixel Gaussian and kept where the blur stays above 0.999, about 3σ (2.5 cm) clear of the body's edge and of every rod
noise σthe standard deviation, over the water region, of the measured VMI minus the noise-free reference: the noise alone, without the phantom's own nonuniformity
dual_results = let
    mask = phantom_cpu.mask[:, :, size(phantom_cpu.mask, 3) ÷ 2]
    water_mask = collect(BS.erode_mask_2d(
        mask .== UInt8(BS.REGION_SOLID_WATER);
        erode_px = 12.0,
    ))
    rod_labels = (
        Ca = UInt8.((10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16)),
        I = UInt8.((20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26)),
    )
    rod_names = (
        Ca = (
            "50 mg/mL",
            "100 mg/mL",
            "200 mg/mL",
            "300 mg/mL",
            "400 mg/mL",
            "500 mg/mL",
            "600 mg/mL",
        ),
        I = (
            "2.0 mg/mL",
            "2.5 mg/mL",
            "5.0 mg/mL",
            "7.5 mg/mL",
            "10.0 mg/mL",
            "15.0 mg/mL",
            "20.0 mg/mL",
        ),
    )
    function rod_roi(label)
        pixels = findall(==(label), mask)
        cx = mean(pixel -> Float64(pixel[1]), pixels)
        cy = mean(pixel -> Float64(pixel[2]), pixels)
        [
            CartesianIndex(i, j)
            for j in max(1, floor(Int, cy - 8)):min(size(mask, 2), ceil(Int, cy + 8))
            for i in max(1, floor(Int, cx - 8)):min(size(mask, 1), ceil(Int, cx + 8))
            if (i - cx)^2 + (j - cy)^2 ≤ 64
        ]
    end
    energies = Float64.(dual_vmi.energies)
    vmi(stack, index) = view(stack.vmis, :, :, :, index)
    region(volume, pixels) = [volume[p, z] for z in axes(volume, 3) for p in pixels]
    μwater = Dict(E => BS.compute_μ_at_energy(BS.XA.Materials.water, E) for E in energies)
    rods = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
    for group in (:Ca, :I)
        measured = zeros(length(rod_labels[group]), length(energies))
        reference = similar(measured)
        theoretical = similar(measured)
        for (row, label) in pairs(rod_labels[group])
            roi = rod_roi(label)
            material = phantom_cpu.materials[Int(label) + 1]
            for (column, E) in pairs(energies)
                measured[row, column] = mean(region(vmi(dual_vmi, column), roi))
                reference[row, column] = mean(region(vmi(reference_vmi, column), roi))
                μ = BS.compute_μ_at_energy(material, E)
                theoretical[row, column] = 1000 * (μ - μwater[E]) / μwater[E]
            end
        end
        rods[group] = (names = rod_names[group], measured, reference, theoretical)
    end
    water_pixels = findall(water_mask)
    water(stack, k) = region(vmi(stack, k), water_pixels)
    (
        energies,
        water_mask,
        rods,
        water_mean = [mean(water(dual_vmi, k)) for k in eachindex(energies)],
        water_mean_reference = [mean(water(reference_vmi, k)) for k in eachindex(energies)],
        water_noise = [
            std(water(dual_vmi, k) .- water(reference_vmi, k))
            for k in eachindex(energies)
        ],
        finite = all(isfinite, dual_vmi.vmis) && all(isfinite, reference_vmi.vmis),
    )
end;

The Solid Water

The eroded solid-water region (left) and its mean HU at each energy, measured and noise-free. The phantom's solid water has the composition of water, so its theoretical HU is 0 at every energy.

The Noise

The noise is what is left when the noise-free reference is subtracted from the measured VMI (left, at 50 keV, in the water region): the phantom's structure and any deterministic artefact cancel. Its standard deviation is the noise σ at each energy (right).

The Rods against Theory

Each rod is measured in the dashed disk drawn on it (top). Solid lines are the measured HU, crosses the noise-free reference and dashed lines the theoretical HU.

Accuracy against the noise-free reference and against theory. Water: the mean HU of the measured / noise-free VMI, and the noise σ. Rods: the mean absolute error against theory of the measured / noise-free VMI, and the mean and the largest absolute bias of the 14 measured rods against the noise-free reference.

The solid water reads -0.8 / -1.2 / -1.5 / -1.5 HU at 50 / 70 / 100 / 140 keV, within 0.4 HU of the noise-free reference: an offset the reference shares comes from physics the decomposition does not invert exactly (scatter, and the blurs of the focal spot, the detector and the view integration, taken before the log), not from the noise or the denoising. The noise falls from σ = 35.4 HU at 50 keV to 25.9 HU at 140 keV. The largest mean rod error against theory, over both rod groups and every energy, is 40.8 HU measured and 52.1 HU noise-free.

That largest error is the calcium rods at 50 keV, 40.8 HU measured and 52.1 HU noise-free. The noise-free reference has it too, so it is the basis, not the noise or the denoiser: the decomposition writes every material as water plus iodine, which spans calcium's energy dependence only approximately, and least well at low energy, where the photoelectric term dominates. From 70 keV up the calcium error is 1.9 to 15.0 HU.

Linear Regression

The same rods (drawn above), measured HU against theoretical HU at each energy, with the least-squares line. The dashed line is identity, perfect agreement.

checks = let

    addcheck(
        "both kVp channels in the likelihood",
        dual_vmi.settings.n_channels,
        dual_vmi.settings.n_channels == 2,
    )

        (
            dual_vmi.settings.denoiser !== nothing,
            dual_vmi.settings.acnr !== nothing,
            dual_vmi.settings.recon.filter isa BS.PairFilter,
        ),
        dual_vmi.settings.denoiser !== nothing &&
            dual_vmi.settings.acnr !== nothing &&
            dual_vmi.settings.recon.filter isa BS.PairFilter,

    addcheck(
        "measured and reference share the pair",

        dual_vmi.settings.pair.basis == reference_vmi.settings.pair.basis,
    )
    addcheck("all VMI values finite", dual_results.finite, dual_results.finite)
    water_worst = maximum(abs, dual_results.water_mean)
    addcheck(
        "solid-water worst absolute HU",
        round(water_worst, digits = 2),
        water_worst ≤ 10,
    )
    list
end;
